71838.subject: Biology
71838.question_text: Which of the following organisms contains Chlorophyll in its cells?
71838.explanation: Some species of Euglena have chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is found in the chloroplasts of Euglena, which are organelles that perform photosynthesis. Euglena are unicellular organisms that can be photosynthetic or heterotrophic. When there is enough sunlight, Euglena use chlorophyll a and b to produce sugars through photosynthesis.

71840.subject: Biology
71840.explanation: A specie is a group of organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring. Species are the most basic unit of biological classification.

options.text: are of different origins and are always found together
are of common origin but cannot interbreed freely
have similar features and can interbreed freely
resemble each other and occupy different niches

71863.subject: Biology
71863.question_text: A plant with short, vertical underground stem is a
71863.explanation: A corm is a short, vertical, swollen underground stem of a plant that acts as a storage organ for food, typically starches, allowing the plant to survive through unfavorable conditions like winter or drought; essentially, it's a solid, fleshy bulb-like structure that differs from a true bulb by lacking layered scales and being entirely solid tissue inside; common examples of plants that grow from corms include crocus, gladiolus, and freesia.

71865.subject: Biology
71865.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of a reproductive process in an organism. Study it and answer ques tions 4 and 5.

The type of reproduction illustrated is
71865.explanation: The type of reproduction illustrated is binary fission.Binary fission is a type of asexual reproduction where a cell splits into two identical daughter cells. It's the primary method of reproduction for prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and archaea.

71867.subject: Biology
71867.question_text: The illustrated organism is capable of reproducing by
71867.explanation: The illustrated organism is paramecium.Paramecium primarily reproduces asexually through a process called binary fission, where a single cell splits into two identical daughter cells; however, they can also reproduce sexually through a process called conjugation under certain conditions.

71869.subject: Biology
71869.question_text: Which of the following organisms consists of unicellular cells joined to form a filament?
71869.explanation: Spirogyra cells join together to form filaments. Spirogyra is a green algae that forms long, unbranched filaments. The filaments are made up of many cylindrical cells that are connected end-to-end. Spirogyra are unicellular organisms that connect to form multicellular filaments. To become long filaments, single spirogyra cells link together, end-to-end, forming strands up to several centimeters in length.

71871.subject: Biology
71871.question_text: The structure in the cell that controls the movement of substances in and out of the cell is the
71871.explanation:
The cell membrane, also known as the plasma membrane, controls the movement of substances in and out of a cell. "cytoplasmic membrane" is the same as "cell membrane"; they are both terms used to describe the outer boundary of a cell that separates the cell's interior from the external environment, and it's also sometimes called the "plasma membrane". 

  • The cell membrane is a semipermeable lipid bilayer that surrounds the cell. 
  • It separates the inside of the cell from the outside environment. 
  • The cell membrane is selectively permeable, meaning it allows some substances to pass through but not others. 
  • The cell membrane regulates the transport of materials entering and exiting the cell.

71873.subject: Biology
71873.question_text: The bursting of a red blood cell placed  in a hypotonic solution is called
71873.explanation:
The bursting of a red blood cell placed in a hypotonic solution is called haemolysis. 

A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell's contents. When a red blood cell is placed in a hypotonic solution, water moves into the cell.This causes the cell to swell and eventually burst.The process of a cell swelling and bursting is called haemolysis. 

  • Isotonic: An environment where the flow of water in and out of a cell is equal. 
  • Osmosis: The movement of water across a semipermeable membrane. Osmosis is important in maintaining homeostasis, which is the tendency of systems toward a relatively stable dynamic equilibrium. 
  • Crenation: The process of a red blood cell shrinking in size when placed in a hypertonic solution.

71876.subject: Biology
71876.question_text: The function of the root hair in plants is to
71876.explanation: Root hairs in plants absorb water and nutrients from the soil and anchor the plant in the soil. Root hairs are threadlike cells that grow between soil particles. They increase the surface area of the root, allowing it to absorb more water.

options.text: absorb soil water by the process of osmosis.
excrete water and mineral salts by simple diffusion.
purify the soil for the plant.

71878.subject: Biology
71878.question_text: If a germinating seed is attached horizontally to a revolving klinostat, what would be the effect on the seedling after three days? The
71878.explanation: If a germinating seed is attached horizontally to a revolving klinostat, the seedling will grow in a random or unpredictable direction, rather than the upward direction towards light (phototropism) or downward direction towards gravity (geotropism). This is because the klinostat constantly rotates, eliminating any consistent gravitational or light direction. As a result, the seedling's growth will not be influenced by these environmental cues, leading to a more disordered growth pattern, making the plumule and the radicle not showing any curvature.

options.text: plumule will curve vertically upward while the radicle will not show any curvature
radicle will curve towards the ground while the plumule will not show any curvature.
plumule and radicle will not show any curvature.
plumule will curve vertically upwards while the radicle will curve towards the ground

71880.subject: Biology
71880.question_text: The lumbar vertebra differs from the thoracic vertebra because it possesses a
71880.explanation:
The correct answer is C. Thicker centrum.

Lumbar vertebrae have several distinct features that differentiate them from thoracic vertebrae. Some of these features include:

- Thicker and more robust centrum (vertebral body)

- Shorter and more sturdy transverse processes

- No costal facets (since lumbar vertebrae do not articulate with ribs)

- Larger and more triangular vertebral foramen

In contrast, thoracic vertebrae typically have:

- Longer and thinner transverse processes

- Costal facets for articulation with ribs

- Smaller vertebral foramen

So, while options A and D are partially correct, the most distinctive feature of lumbar vertebrae is their thicker centrum.

71881.subject: Biology
71881.question_text: Which of the following blood vessels carries oxygenated blood into the heart?
71881.explanation:
The pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart. All veins carries deoxygenated blood except pulmonary vein which carries oxygenated blood to the heart.

Conversely, all arteries carry oxygenated blood except the pulmonary artery that carries deoxygenated blood.

71883.subject: Biology
71883.question_text: Filtrates in the Bowman's capsule contain vitamins because
71883.explanation: Filtrates in the Bowman's capsule contain vitamins because the filtration process in the kidney allows small molecules like vitamins to pass through from the blood into the Bowman's capsule, while larger molecules like proteins are retained in the bloodstream; essentially, the filtrate is composed of blood plasma minus the large proteins, which means it includes most of the small molecules present in the blood, including vitamins.

options.text: most of them are fat soluble.
they cannot be reabsorbed into the blood.
little amount is required by the blood.

71884.subject: Biology
71884.question_text: The structures that contain grey matter and white matter are found in the
71884.explanation: The brain and spinal cord contain gray matter and white matter. The two make up the CNS. In the spinal cord, white matter sits external to the gray matter, while it lies deeper to the gray matter of the cerebral cortex, the outer layer of the brain.

71887.subject: Biology
71887.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of sense organ in humans. Study it and answer questions 15 and 16. 

The part that protects the organ is labelled
71887.explanation:
The parts labelled are:

I - IRIS

II - EYE LASHES

III - PUPIL

IV - SCLERA

The sclera, cornea, eyelids, eyelashes, and bony orbit all protect the eye from injury. 

Sclera - labelled IV

  • The tough, white, fibrous tissue that surrounds the eyeball
  • Helps maintain the eye's shape
  • Protects the eye from injury
  • Extends from the cornea to the optic nerve at the back of the eye

Cornea 

  • The clear, curved layer in front of the iris and pupil
  • Protects the front of the eye
  • Helps focus light on the retina at the back of the eye

Eyelids 

  • Thin flaps of skin and muscle that can cover the eye
  • Reflexively close quickly (blink) to protect the eye from foreign objects, wind, dust, insects, and very bright light

Eyelashes - labelled II

  • Short, tough hairs that grow from the edge of the eyelid
  • Keep insects and foreign particles away from the eye

71891.subject: Biology
71891.explanation:
The parts labelled are:

I - Iris

II - Eye lashes

III - Pupil

IV - Sclera

71892.subject: Biology
71892.question_text:
The diagram above is an illustration of two plants P and Q. Arrows I, II and III illustrate the transfer of pollen grains among flowers of plants P and  Q. Studly it and answer questions 17 and 18.

The types of pollination illustrated as I,Il and III, respectively are
71892.explanation:
I - Self pollination

II - Self pollination

III - Cross pollination

Self-pollination occurs when pollen grains are transferred from anther to the stigma within the same flower(as seen in I) or plant(as seen in II), while cross-pollination occurs when pollen grains are transferred from the anther of a plant to the stigma of another plant of the same species(as seen in III).

71893.subject: Biology
71893.question_text: The condition necessary for reproduction to occur between plants P and Q after pollination is that plants P and Q should be
71893.explanation: The condition necessary for reproduction to occur between plants P and Q after pollination is that plants P and Q must be of the same species.

71894.subject: Biology
71894.question_text:
The diagram above illustrates a dry dehiscent fruit. Use it to answer questions 19 and 20. 

The agent of dispersal of the fruit is
71894.explanation: The dehiscent fruit is the Tridax. The Tridax procumbens plant's seeds are dispersed by the wind because they have a pappus, which is a feathery appendage. The pappus's adhesion power allows the seeds to cling to the hairs of animals or clothing.

71895.subject: Biology
71895.question_text: The Parachute-like tuft of hairs developed from the
71895.explanation: The parachute-like tuft of hairs found in Tridax develops from the calyx (modified sepals).

71896.subject: Biology
71896.question_text: Which of the following events does not occur in the light reaction stage of photosynthesis?
71896.explanation: In the light stage of photosynthesis, the key events include: chlorophyll absorbing light energy, excited electrons being transferred through electron transport chains, water splitting to release oxygen, and the generation of ATP and NADPH molecules using the captured energy from light; all of these processes occur within the thylakoid membranes of chloroplasts. However, Carbon(IV) oxide does not combine with hydrogen in the light stage.

71897.subject: Biology
71897.question_text: The rate of photosynthesis decreases in a wilted herbaceous plant because the
71897.explanation:
Wilting occurs when a plant loses more water through transpiration than it absorbs from the soil.To prevent further water loss, the stomata on the leaves close. When the stomata are closed,CO\(_2\) can't enter the leaf. CO\(_2\) is essential for photosynthesis, which produces glucose and oxygen. 

The rate of photosynthesis decreases in a wilted herbaceous plant because the stomata close, preventing carbon dioxide (CO\(_2\)) from entering the leaf.

options.text: enzymes in the leaf were denatured
chlorophyll in the leaves was not broken down
amount of light reaching the plant was reduced
amount of carbon dioxide entering the leaf decrease.

71898.subject: Biology
71898.question_text: The element required for chlorophyll formation in plants is
71898.explanation:
The elements needed for chlorophyll formation in plants are iron, magnesium, and nitrogen. 

Explanation

  • Iron: Helps synthesize chlorophyll and maintains the structure of chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll 
  • Magnesium: An essential component of chlorophyll, which is a vital pigment for photosynthesis 
  • Nitrogen: Helps plants produce chlorophyll 

Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plants and algae. It's essential for photosynthesis, which is the process by which plants convert light energy, carbon dioxide, and water into sugar and oxygen.

71899.subject: Biology
71899.question_text: The process of food digestion in mammals would
71899.explanation:
Digestion in mammals breaks down food into nutrients that the body uses for energy, growth, and repair. 

How digestion works 

  1. Ingestion: Food is taken in.
  2. Mastication: Food is chewed and mixed with saliva.
  3. Secretion: Digestive juices are released into the digestive tract.
  4. Digestion: Food is broken down into smaller molecules.
  5. Absorption: Nutrients, water, vitamins, and electrolytes are absorbed into the bloodstream.
  6. Evacuation: Waste products are eliminated.

options.text: make energy immediately available to the body
promote growth and repair of tissues
provide sufficient food materials within the body
render food substances soluble and absorbable

71900.subject: Biology
71900.question_text: Which of the following food substances would give a negative reaction with Benedict's reagent?
71900.explanation: Benedict's reagent is used to test for the presence of reducing sugars in a sample, like glucose, by changing colour from blue to green, yellow, orange, or red depending on the concentration of the sugar present; a positive result indicates the presence of a reducing sugar and is shown by a brick-red precipitate forming. Fructose, glucose and galactose are reducing sugar but sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

71901.subject: Biology
71901.explanation: Sunlight is the primary source of light and heat on Earth. It's also a major source of energy, vitamin D, and contributes to climate and weather patterns.

71902.subject: Biology
71902.question_text: Discouraging the use of poison to kill fish in a large water body is a way of
71902.explanation: Discouraging the use of poison to kill fish in a large water body is a way of conserving the fish species. Poisons can be used in water bodies to control fish populations, but they can also contaminate water and harm aquatic life.

options.text: allowing the fittest organism to survive
making the fish adapt to their environment

71903.subject: Biology
71903.question_text: The pathway through which nutrient are replenished and circulated in an ecosystem is called a
71903.explanation: The pathway through which nutrients are replenished and circulated in an ecosystem is called a biogeochemical cycle. Biogeochemical cycles are also known as nutrient cycles.They describe how chemical elements move through the atmosphere, soil, rocks, water, and organisms.

71904.subject: Biology
71904.question_text:
The illustration below is a food chain. Study it and answer questions 29 and 30.
             Grasses → Grasshoppers → Lizards → Hawks

Which of the following statements is not correct about the food chain? The number of
71904.explanation: In a food chain, energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next, with each level typically having fewer individual than the previous ones.In a food chain, producers have more energy than primary consumers. Producers are the first level in a food chain, and they produce their own food using energy from the sun. Primary consumers are the next level up in the food chain, and they eat the producers.

options.text: grasses eaten by grasshoppers is greater than the number of grasshoppers.
grasses eaten by grasshoppers is fewer than the number of grasshoppers.

grasshoppers eaten by lizards is greater than the number
of lizards.
lizards eaten by hawks is greater than the number of hawks.

71905.subject: Biology
71905.question_text:
Grasses → Grasshoppers → Lizards  → Hawks

If the individual species of organisms in the food chain are counted and arranged as a pyramid, the result would be a pyramid of
71905.explanation: A pyramid of numbers is a diagram that shows the number of organisms at each level of a food chain. It's a bar chart with stacked bars, where the width of each bar represents the number of organisms. Pyramids of number show the number of organisms at each stage in a food chain. Pyramids of biomass show the mass of organisms at each stage in a food chain.

71906.subject: Biology
71906.question_text: Which of the following gases is released during the decomposition of organic matter?
71906.explanation:
The primary gas released during the decomposition of organic matter is carbon dioxide (CO\(_2\)) 

When organic matter decomposes, the primary gases released are carbon dioxide(CO\(_2\))  and methane (CH\(_4\)), with carbon dioxide being produced in both aerobic (with oxygen) and anaerobic (without oxygen) conditions, while methane is primarily produced in anaerobic environments like landfills. 

Other gases that may be released during decomposition include:

  • Hydrogen sulfide (H2S): This gas has a strong, rotten egg smell and is produced in anaerobic conditions. 
  • Nitrogen gas (N2): Released as a byproduct of the breakdown of organic nitrogen compounds.

71907.subject: Biology
71907.question_text:
The diagrams above are the illustrations of organisms from different habitat. Study them and answer questions 32 and 33.

The structures labelled I are for
71907.explanation: The shell of snail and the spines of a cactus both serve as physical defenses. The shell of the snail protects it from predators and physical harm in the environment while the spine of the cactus prevents water loss and also prevent the cactus from being eaten by herbivores.

71908.subject: Biology
71908.explanation: Snails live all over the world in soil (or dirt), sand, trees, under rocks or leaves, and in the rivers, lakes, and oceans. Land snails cannot breathe under water so they must come out when too much water enters their habitat to avoid drowning. The habitat of the cactus plant is dry, arid deserts. Most plants would die in the intense heat and sunlight that are present here, but cacti have adaptations that allow them to thrive.

71909.subject: Biology
71909.question_text: An environmental problem caused by Sulphur (IV) oxide is
71909.explanation: Sulphur dioxide SO\(_2\) can cause many environmental problems, including acid rain, smog, and damage to plants. When SO\(_2\) combines with water and air, it forms sulfuric acid, which is the main component of acid rain. Acid rain damages plants and trees, and can kill fish and other aquatic specie.

71910.subject: Biology
71910.question_text: The phenomenon by which a farmland that is left to fallow for several years develops into a forest is called
71910.explanation: The process by which a fallow farm field develops into a forest is called ecological succession. This is when natural communities replace one another over time. In ecological succession, an abandoned farm field will first become a meadow, then bushes, and eventually a forest. This process can take many years.

Which of the following effects would not be observed among the population of the plants?
71912.explanation: Overpopulation would definitely leads to rise in disease condition, death and competition among the organisms but there won't be any mutualistic relationship.

71914.subject: Biology
71914.question_text:
The bar chart above shows the data of sources of energy used for cooking in a community. Study it and answer questions 37 and 38.

The source of energy that is mostly used in the community is
71914.explanation: Kerosene has the longest bar, showing the highest number of households.

71915.subject: Biology
71915.question_text: The two sources of energy that would mostly lead to pollution in the community are
71915.explanation: Burning kerosene and coal can cause significant air and water pollution, as well as climate change. Burning kerosene releases carbon dioxide (CO2), particulate matter, nitrogen oxides (NOx), and sulfur oxides (SOx). These emissions contribute to climate change and degrade air quality. Also, burning coal releases harmful air pollutants, including benzene, formaldehyde, and carbon monoxide.

71916.subject: Biology
71916.question_text: An individual found a strange bird that is tagged as an endangered specie. What should the individual do?
71916.explanation: The individual should return the endangered bird to its natural habitat, which will ensure conservation and in turn restore population ans preserve ecosystem balance, so the specie doesn't go into extinction.

options.text: Take it to an aquatic environment
Return it to its natural habitat
Sell it at a very high price

71918.subject: Biology
71918.question_text: Which of the following traits is not inheritable? Ability to
71918.explanation: Simply "rolling the eyeball" as a conscious gesture is not considered an inheritable trait, as it's primarily a learned behaviour and not directly coded in our genes; however, certain involuntary eye movements like "nystagmus" can be genetic and manifest as eye rolling in some situations, meaning there could be a hereditary component in specific cases related to eye movement.

71919.subject: Biology
71919.question_text: Which of the following statements is correct about the ABO blood group system?
71919.explanation:
In the ABO blood group system, antibodies are located in the plasma, which is the liquid part of blood. 

  • The ABO blood group system is based on the presence of antigens and antibodies in the blood. 
  • Antigens are protein molecules on the surface of red blood cells. 
  • Antibodies are proteins in the plasma that recognize foreign substances.

options.text: Antigens are located on the surface of white blood cells
Antibodies are located in the blood plasma
Antibodies are located on the surface of the red blood cells
Antigens are located in the blood plasma

71920.subject: Biology
71920.question_text: A woman with blood group A gives birth to a child with blood group O. Which of the following blood groups cannot belong to the father?
71920.explanation: A woman with blood group A and a man with blood group AB can never produce a child with blood group O. Blood group A could either be from AA homozygous or AO heterozygous.

71924.subject: Biology
71924.question_text: The physical appearance of an organism is described as its
71924.explanation:
The physical appearance of an organism is described as its phenotype. A phenotype refers to the observable characteristics of an organism, including its physical traits, which are determined by its genotype (genetic makeup) and can be influenced by environmental factors. 

Genotype is the genetic makeup of an organism or person, which is determined by their DNA sequence. It can also refer to the alleles, or variant forms of a gene, that an organism has.

71925.subject: Biology
71925.explanation: Mutation leads to evolution by introducing genetic variations within a population, which natural selection can then act upon, favouring individuals with advantageous mutations that allow them to survive and reproduce more successfully, thus passing on those beneficial traits to future generations, gradually changing the characteristics of the population over time and leading to evolution; essentially, mutations are the raw material for evolution, providing the diversity needed for natural selection to operate.

options.text: kills all organisms where it has occurred.
gives rise to offspring having same characteristics as the parents
does not confer adaptability to the offspring
gives rise to new individuals that differ from their parents

71927.subject: Biology
71927.question_text: The male and female gametes which bear genes for inheritance in plants are located in the
71927.explanation:
In flowering plants, male gametes are in the anthers and female gametes are in the ovules.

  • Male gametes

    • Located in pollen grains
    • Produced in the anthers of the flower
    • Part of the stamen, the male structure of the flower

  • Female gametes

    • Located in ovules
    • Produced in the ovary of the flower
    • Part of the pistil, the female structure of the flower

71933.subject: Biology
71933.question_text: Which type of breeding is represented by industrial melanism in peppered moths?
71933.explanation:
Industrial melanism in peppered moths is an example of evolution by natural selection. It occurred when the colour of the peppered moth population changed in response to air pollution from coal-burning factories during the Industrial Revolution. 

The common pale form of the peppered moth was replaced by a previously unknown black form. The dark moths were better able to blend in with the darkened bark of trees, while the pale moths were more visible to predators. The dark form became more common, and in some areas of England, the original pale form was almost lost by the end of the 19th century.
